info.title: Servana Admin API — the legacy surface, as mounted
info.description:
Every /api/admin/* operation the app mounts. GENERATED from the route tree by
`npm run admin:docs` — do not edit by hand.

READ THIS BEFORE GENERATING A CLIENT.

These routes are NOT exempt from `parityMiddleware`. Unless x-parity-rewritten is
false, the wire carries ADDITIONAL alias keys this document does not declare —
first_name, providerUid, level2, photoURL and some forty more, injected on the way
out. So a declared shape here is a SUBSET of what arrives, never the whole of it.
That is the opposite of openapi.v1.json, whose shapes are exactly the wire.

An operation whose 200 payload reads "UNSPECIFIED" has a real shape that nobody has
written down yet. It is deliberately not guessed: a wrong schema is worse than an
absent one, because a client generates types from it and breaks in a way that looks
like the backend is at fault.

messageBody.description: LEFT JOINed from chat_messages, so null when the message is gone.

OnboardingQueueSummary.description: The onboarding queue, counted in one pass. Providers only — role 2 or 4, not archived. Every value is an integer.

newSubmissions.description: Counts a provider with NO case row as well as one whose status is `submitted`. A provider who has never been triaged is a new submission, not an absence.

highPriority.description: high OR urgent, and only for cases not already approved, rejected, withdrawn or expired — a closed case cannot be urgent.

unassigned.description: No reviewer, and only in submitted / queued / in_review.

OnboardingCaseRow.description: One row of the onboarding queue list.

caseId.description: NULL for a provider who has no case row yet — see newSubmissions.

fullName.description: First and last joined and trimmed, FALLING BACK TO THE EMAIL when both are empty.

onboardingStatus.description: Defaults to 'not_started' when no case row exists.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency token. Pass it as expectedVersion when moving the case.

OnboardingCaseDetail.description: Everything a reviewer needs on one screen.

requirements.description: Uploaded requirements with their current decision.

pendingApplications.description: Service applications in pending_review, counted in JS from the same rows.

OnboardingReadiness.description: Whether this provider could be approved right now. COMPUTED ON READ, never stored, so it is a statement about the moment you asked.

warningCount.description: Blockers of severity `warning`. These do NOT count toward blockingCount.

blockers.description: Each carries a severity; only the non-warning ones block approval.

allRequirementsApproved.description: FALSE when the provider has uploaded NOTHING — the predicate is `reqs.length > 0 && every(approved)`, so an empty set is not vacuously true. That is deliberate: a provider with no documents is not a provider with all documents approved.

summary.description: The counts behind the checks, so a reviewer sees why rather than only what.

OnboardingCaseNote.description: A case note as the LIST route returns it — camelCase, author name joined.

isProviderVisible.description: The disclosure gate. The list returns internal notes by default, so a client that ignores this field will show a provider what reviewers said about them.

authorName.description: Falls back to 'Admin' when the join finds no name.

OnboardingCaseNoteRaw.description: The note as the CREATE route returns it: the raw INSERT row, SNAKE_CASE, no mapper. The list route on the same entity answers camelCase. Documented as it stands.

OnboardingCaseRaw.description: A provider_onboarding_cases row as `transitionCase` returns it — raw, SNAKE_CASE, no mapper. Contrast OnboardingCaseDetail.case, which is the camelCased projection of the same table.

version.description: Already incremented by this transition. Use THIS value as the next expectedVersion.

OnboardingTimelineEvent.description: One audited step in a case history.

providerMessage.description: What the PROVIDER was told, as distinct from the internal rationale.

actorName.description: Falls back to 'System' for an unattributed step.

OnboardingReasonCode.description: One entry in the decision vocabulary. assertValidReasonCode refuses any code not in this table, so a client should populate its picker from here rather than hard-code.

applicableDecisions.description: Coalesced to []. Which decisions this code may accompany.

requiresFreeText.description: The reviewer must add their own words.

providerMayResubmit.description: What separates a request-resubmission from a rejection.

RequirementDecisionResult.description: The recorded decision, plus two flags about what happened AFTER it. The row half is a raw INSERT ... RETURNING *, so those keys are SNAKE_CASE; the two flags are camelCase because the service adds them. One object, two naming conventions — documented as it stands.

decision.description: Constrained by a CHECK on the table, so no other value can be stored.

internal_rationale.description: REVIEWER-ONLY. Never show this to a provider; provider_message is their copy.

is_superseded.description: Decisions are APPEND-ONLY: a later decision supersedes an earlier one rather than replacing it, so the history of a requirement is recoverable.

providerNotified.description: Whether the provider was actually told. FALSE is a real outcome — the decision stands and the notification did not go out.

lifecycleSynchronized.description: Whether the provider account lifecycle was updated to match this decision.

AdminProviderMetrics.description: Provider counts for the admin dashboard, from one query plus several helpers. TWO FIELDS CAN BE -1. providersMissingAvailability and providersMissingServiceArea are counted through safeCount and safeMongoCount, whose contract is stated in the service: "-1 means could not be established, NEVER zero". Rendering -1 as 0 turns "we cannot read that table" into "everything is fine", which is the reading that costs the most.

providersWithBothActiveServiceAndPending.description: Deduped: a provider counted here is in both of the two above.

providersMissingAvailability.description: -1 MEANS UNKNOWN, not zero. Counted through safeCount, which returns -1 when the table is absent or its schema does not match.

providersMissingServiceArea.description: -1 MEANS UNKNOWN, not zero. This one spans MongoDB — worker_locations is not in Postgres, and reaching for it through safeCount is how it silently read -1 for the life of the function.

AdminProviderIdentity.description: A provider as the 360 detail screen reads them. Assembled across user_credentials, the profile and address tables, the availability state and the MongoDB location document — so a null here can mean "not recorded" or "that store had nothing".

fullName.description: Joined and trimmed, FALLING BACK TO THE EMAIL when both names are empty.

role.description: A NUMBER — Number(cred.role). 2 and 4 are both provider roles.

birthdate.description: A DATE — no zone, deliberately unparsed.

address.description: NULL when addressOne is empty — the whole object is withheld rather than returned with null fields, so a client tests the object, not each field.

onlineStatus.description: From the MongoDB location document. 'offline' is also what an ABSENT document yields, so it does not distinguish "logged off" from "never seen".

lastSeenAt.description: From MongoDB, so it does NOT pass through the Postgres UTC parser.

ProviderServiceApplication.description: A provider request to be granted a service.

category.description: Always '' on this route — the query selects a literal empty string.

reviewedByName.description: NULL when the reviewer join found nothing, not when there was no reviewer.

ProviderRequirementRow.description: One uploaded requirement document, as the LIST returns it. Read fileUrl and legacyStorage together before rendering anything.

fileUrl.description: NULL for every canonically-stored document, ALWAYS. The service withholds it deliberately: "canonical private rows never leak signed URLs through list responses". A non-null value here means a LEGACY row that keeps its compatibility URL until the controlled backfill. Use the preview endpoint to obtain a URL, and do not treat null as "no document" — read previewAvailable.

previewExpiresAt.description: ALWAYS null on the list. A constant, not a signal — the list issues no preview.

previewAvailable.description: True when EITHER a canonical storage path or a legacy URL exists. This is the "is there a document" field.

legacyStorage.description: True when there is no canonical storage path.

byteSize.description: Number()d, so a bigint column arrives as a number.

scanState.description: The malware scan state, coalesced to 'legacy_review_required' — which means NOT SCANNED, not "clean". A legacy row has never been through the scanner.

identifierMask.description: A MASKED identifier. The full value is never projected to an admin list.

AdminProviderJobRow.description: One job in a provider history, as the admin list projects it.

id.description: A STRING, and the SAME value as bookingId.

bookingId.description: A STRING here, though the v1 surface types booking ids as integers.

bookingCode.description: Derived, SVN-XXXXXX. Not a stored column.

customerName.description: DELIBERATELY MASKED: first name plus the INITIAL of the surname, e.g. "Maria S.". A provider job history is not a customer directory, and the full surname is not projected here even for an admin.

completionRate.description: A WHOLE-NUMBER PERCENTAGE in [0, 100] — 80 means 80%, not 0.8. Rounded. ZERO when totalJobs is 0, which is a division guard rather than a measurement: a provider with no jobs has no completion rate, and 0% reads as failure. Check totalJobs before rendering this. See TAB 05 on rate units.

AdminProviderEarnings.description: The ADMIN earnings view, which discloses gross as well as the provider share.

totalProviderShare.description: providerShareOf(gross) — computed server-side, never by a client.

thisMonthGross.description: The MANILA month. Bounded through services/sql/businessPeriod, so it agrees with getFinanceSummary's paymentsToday and revenueMtd rather than reporting a different month from the next admin screen. It previously truncated on the SESSION timezone, which the pool pins to UTC, so the first eight hours of every Manila month were counted in the previous one.

providerSharePercent.description: A WHOLE-NUMBER PERCENT in [0, 100]. NOT a fraction — contrast BookingPayment.servana.commissionRate on the v1 surface, which is a fraction in [0, 1]. One split, two representations, a hundredfold apart. See TAB 05.

AdminProviderTimeOff.description: A worker_time_off row as the ADMIN route returns it: SELECT *, no mapper, so the keys are SNAKE_CASE. The v1 ProviderTimeOff schema describes the same table in camelCase — two shapes for one entity, documented rather than reconciled.

id.description: A NUMBER. The column is integer; TAB 07 corrected the v1 contract, which claimed string.

status.description: Cancelling does NOT delete the row, so this list includes cancelled periods.

ProviderAutoOnlineReadiness.description: Whether this provider can be brought online automatically, and what is stopping it. Evaluated on READ — autoOnline.lastEvaluatedAt is the moment you asked, not a stored fact. Typed as ProviderAutoOnlineReadiness in providerAutoOnlineEngine.

source.description: Where this provider came from, and how confident that is.

sourceConfidence.description: 'inferred' means it was deduced, not recorded — do not report it as fact.

requiredTotal.description: A CONSTANT of 3 in the engine.

classification.description: 'legacy_inferred' means the types were deduced from older rows.

source.description: WHICH store the association was found in. `mixed` means more than one, and they may disagree.

active.description: Auto-online is switched on for them.

bookable.description: The one that decides whether work can reach them. Eligible and active are inputs to it.

availabilityMode.description: 'missing' is not 'always available' — it means nothing was configured.

lastEvaluatedAt.description: The moment THIS request evaluated it. Never a stored value.

warnings.description: Do NOT prevent bookability. Rendering these as blockers overstates the problem.

AuditListItem.description: One audit event as the lists project it. Every field is stringified or defaulted by rowToListItem.

displayTime.description: A PRE-RENDERED Manila local time string, beside the ISO occurredAt. Two representations of one instant: render this, compute with occurredAt. Do not parse displayTime — it is display text, not a timestamp.

actionLabel.description: Human-readable, FALLING BACK to the raw action when unmapped.

summary.description: Composed server-side from action, outcome, entity and actor.

severity.description: Computed from the action and its outcome, not stored.

requestId.description: THE JOIN KEY. Filterable via ?request_id=, which is how an operator turns a quoted reference into the action that produced it. See TAB 09.

after.description: State AFTER. Null when it deleted something.

request.description: How the action arrived. This is the block an operator joins a quoted id against.

actorLabel.description: Falls back to the uid, then to 'System'.

readAt.description: NULL means unread. This is the field, not a boolean.

AdminUserRow.description: One account of ANY role — customer, provider or admin.

fullName.description: Joined from the parts that exist. EMPTY STRING when neither does — it does NOT fall back to the email, unlike the provider and onboarding lists, which do.

role.description: A NUMBER. 1 admin, 2 and 4 provider, 3 customer.

reference.description: The PUBLIC reference, which is what a provider quotes.

categoryTitle.description: The PROVIDER-facing category title, from provider_title.

internalState.description: What the queue runs on. NOT provider-facing.

The RAW case row is spread at the top level — so those keys are SNAKE_CASE — with `caseId` added as a camelCase string alongside, and eight raw child collections attached. One object, two naming conventions, and the children are unmapped query rows.

caseId.description: Added by the service beside the raw case_id it duplicates.

internalNotes.description: REVIEWER-ONLY. Never render these beside messages — they are not provider-facing.

attachments.description: Metadata only. Use the preview endpoint for a URL.

ProfilePhotoSubmission.description: One profile-photo submission awaiting or past review.

scanState.description: The malware scan result. Not the same thing as the review state.

publishedUrl.description: NULL unless state is exactly `approved` — the presenter gates it on that, so an unapproved submission never leaks a public URL through the list. Null here means "not approved", NOT "no image": use the preview endpoint to look at one.

ProviderAttribution.description: Where a provider came from. Every field prefers a STORED value and falls back to a freshly inferred one, so this object mixes recorded fact with deduction — registrationConfidence is the field that says which.

registrationConfidence.description: 'inferred' means deduced from activity, not declared. Do not report it as declared.

attributionComputedAt.description: NULL when nothing was ever stored — everything above is then inferred live.

ProviderCatalogAssociation.description: How this provider legacy services line up with the canonical catalog. The counts are the adoption measure for retiring the legacy fallback.

status.description: 'not_applicable' is returned WHOLE when the provider has no services at all — every count is then 0 and services is empty. That is not "fully mapped".

unmappedCount.description: Services with no catalog offering. These exist only through the legacy fallback.

ambiguousCount.description: Services matching MORE THAN ONE offering. Ambiguity outranks everything else in the status calculation, because a provider mapped two ways is not mapped.

status.description: Per-service, and what the aggregate counts are built from.

FinanceSummary.description: The finance dashboard, in one pass.

paymentsToday.description: Net of refunds — SUM(amount - refunded_amount) — and bounded by a day computed AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila' EXPLICITLY, not by the UTC session zone. That makes this "today" the operator's today. Contrast AdminProviderEarnings.thisMonthGross, which now uses the SAME definition via services/sql/businessPeriod. It previously truncated on the session zone and therefore reported a UTC month, so the two screens disagreed for the first eight hours of every Manila month. PHP major units.

revenueMtd.description: Month to date, also Manila-bounded, also net of refunds. EXCLUDES synthetic bookings: a smoke-test booking carrying a price would otherwise report as money never taken. PHP major units.

openExceptionCount.description: Reconciliation breaks not yet resolved or ignored. NON-ZERO means the ledger and the payments disagree about money.

RefundAcknowledgement.description: The receipt for a refund transition. Deliberately NOT the whole review, and deliberately carrying no amount: the service is typed Promise<void> and the controller builds this, so there is nothing here to compute with. A caller that needs the record reads it back, rather than this becoming a second and subtly different source for it.

PayoutAcknowledgement.description: The receipt for a payout transition. Same shape of answer as a refund transition, and for the same reason: the service returns void and the state is read back.

byCanonicalState.description: Counts keyed by CANONICAL state. Additive — every legacy field below is unchanged, so a portal that has not migrated reads exactly what it did. Prefer this: the legacy fields cannot express EN_ROUTE or ARRIVED and collapse both into `accepted`.

accepted.description: LEGACY, and lossy: EN_ROUTE and ARRIVED are both counted here.

paymentExceptions.description: ALWAYS ZERO. Hard-coded in the service, not computed. A constant, not a signal — a client rendering "0 payment exceptions" is reporting a literal, and the real answer lives on the finance summary as openExceptionCount.

lateJobs.description: ALWAYS ZERO. Also hard-coded. The admin bookings LIST computes isLate per row at read time, so lateness is knowable — it is simply not aggregated here.

needsAdminAction.description: Derived: new plus awaitingAssignment. Not a separate query.

AdminBookingDetail.description: One booking, assembled from the booking row plus the assignment, add-ons and escalations. Grouped into sub-objects rather than flattened.

operationsStatus.description: LEGACY vocabulary. Cannot express EN_ROUTE or ARRIVED.

stateIsCollapsedInLegacyField.description: True when operationsStatus cannot express canonicalState.

availableActions.description: From the canonical projection, so an action never appears for a state the executor would refuse.

providerAssignment.description: NULL when unassigned. Built from the MOST RECENT booking_workers row — assigned_at DESC LIMIT 1 — so a reassigned booking shows the current provider, not the history.

escalations.description: RAW rows, snake_case — the only unmapped collection in this object.

updatedAt.description: ALWAYS null, hard-coded — the same constant the admin bookings LIST carries. Not "never updated": simply not projected.

PermissionChangePreview.description: A DRY RUN of a permission grant. Nothing is written. It exists so the dependency closure and the risk classification are seen BEFORE the change, rather than found in the audit trail afterwards.

dependenciesAdded.description: Permissions pulled in AUTOMATICALLY because a requested one requires them. These are grants nobody asked for, which is exactly why the preview exists — the effective grant is `toAdd` PLUS this.

criticalPermissions.description: A stricter class than high-risk. Both are about the RESULT, not the delta.

isValid.description: FALSE means the change would be refused. Check this before offering a confirm button.

slug.description: Derived by slugify. The stable handle a URL uses.

status.description: From CATALOG_STATUSES. `archived` rows SURVIVE — they are excluded from reads, not deleted, so an archived deep link resolves to an honest "unavailable" rather than a 404.

displayOrder.description: Set by the reorder route, not by name.

AdminCatalogService.description: One catalog service, with its ancestry denormalised onto the row.

id.description: The CANONICAL services.id — what the eligibility engine keys capability on.

bookable.description: Whether a customer can actually book it. NOT the same as `status: active` — an active service with no provider who can perform it is not bookable, which is what servicesWithoutProviders on the summary counts.

basePriceSummary.description: PRE-RENDERED display text carrying its own peso mark, e.g. "P350 per hour". Not a number and not to be parsed — render basePrice if you need to format it yourself.

MoneyMajorAdmin.description: UNIT: PHP MAJOR units — pesos. CURRENCY: PHP. A real JSON number: catalogAdminService passes it through `money()`, which is `Number(v)`, so it does NOT arrive as the string a numeric column would otherwise yield. See TAB 04.

UtcTimestamp.description: ISO 8601 with a UTC designator, guaranteed at the DRIVER rather than per field: src/db/dbQuery.ts registers asUtcIso against OIDs 1114 (timestamp) and 1184 (timestamptz), and that function ends in Date.toISOString(), which always emits Z. Postgres native "2026-08-11 11:03:23.421016+00" therefore cannot reach a client through this path. See TAB 03.
